b: An agent whose memory an adversary can edit is steerable by curating what it knows. — “you can walk a model past its own line by deleting the context the line depends on”

This is the Fog Attack in a nutshell, and my answer to it is the Guardian Angel Loop Pattern. I built an MCP that allows the web interface Claude (Angel Claude) to peer into a project repository and then i used claude-in-chrome to allow the Claude Code session on my computer (Ward Claude) to peer into the web claude session. The Ward Claude is instructed to be proactive in its reactions to changes in the DOM. The initial impetus for this arrangement was convenience--I wanted the Ward Claude to respond to additions to the plan made by me and the the Angel Claude automatically, without me having to act as a dumb pipe downloading files and pasting the latest updates in claude code's terminal. I wanted to plan with Claude on the go with my phone and not have to wait to get back to my computer for the plan to start running.

The Angel Claude is impervious to fog from the user because its context lives on Anthropic's servers, but it cannot act on the user's machine. The Ward Claude can act on the user's computer, but its context is local to the machine and is thus edit-able. The tandem pair, with eyes on each other, is able to both act and resist a malicious user that edits the Ward Claude's memories or history in order to manufacture consent.
